reason: Hypothesis A directly addresses the limitation of soft ferromagnetism in prior FeCoNiPd/Pt alloys by proposing Mn substitution, which is physically sound due to Mn's antiferromagnetic coupling and lattice strain effects that can pin domain walls. It is specific, testable, and grounded in known magnetic behavior, whereas Hypothesis B incorrectly uses FeCoNi as the baseline instead of the prior Pd/Pt derivatives and relies on Cr substitution evidence from a different alloy system (AlCoFeNi) that may not apply to the required fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy.
